blocks.content: The Constitution envisions the Finance Commission as the balancing wheel of fiscal federalism in India.

rows: Recommends distribution of tax revenues between Centre and States
Acts as a policy think tank for federal and strategic planning
Constituted every 5 years by the President

items: The recommendations made by the Finance Commission are only of an advisory nature and not binding on the government.
The qualification criteria for members are laid down by Parliament through the Finance Commission Act, 1951, not directly detailed in the Constitution.
The Finance Commission submits its report to the President, who places it before both Houses of Parliament along with an action taken memorandum.
The First Finance Commission was constituted in 1951 with K.C. Neogy as its Chairman.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 280 of the Constitution provides for a Finance Commission as a quasi-judicial body.
It is constituted by the President of India every fifth year or at such earlier time as deemed necessary.
Consists of a Chairman and four other members appointed by the President, who are eligible for reappointment.
Parliament is empowered to determine the qualifications of members and the manner in which they are selected.
The Commission acts as the balancing wheel of fiscal federalism in India.
